subject: Payment lanes, apportionment schedule, and VAT trigger thresholds
messages:
From: Ellen Brooks <ellen.brooks@novalabs.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing model question — routing / VAT thresholds

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on — we have a couple of operational asks as we move into the production billing phase for our enterprise rollout. Two points we need your guidance on:

1) We need invoices to be split between Novalabs Inc (US) and Novalabs EU (Ireland) depending on customer seat location. Our finance team wants the split to be visible on the invoice (separate entity lines) rather than a post-billing allocation if possible.

2) VAT trigger thresholds: we expect EU tax exposure to increase as ARR grows. If Redwood routes revenue to the EU entity, what are the suggested VAT trigger thresholds where Novalabs will need local VAT registration (we are currently under some thresholds but expect to cross them in Q3).

Can you share an operational proposal (payment lanes, apportionment schedule, and what info you need from our AP team)? I attached our current contract excerpt and an example mapping file.

Attachments: Nova_contract_v3.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Ellen Brooks
Director, Finance Operations
Novalabs

Laura / Ben — forwarding Ellen's ask. TL;DR: client prefers invoice-level split (preferred by their auditors). They want: entity-specific line items, a monthly apportionment CSV for their ledger, and clear rules for VAT triggers.

Quick thoughts (high level):
- Option A (preferred by client): Invoice-level split at time of issuance. Redwood routes line items to entity A/B and prints two entity blocks on a single PDF invoice. Pros: clean audit trail; cons: requires us to maintain per-customer routing metadata and send separate tax IDs per invoice.
- Option B: Single ledger invoice + monthly internal apportionment (CSV + credit/debit memos). Pros: simpler runtime; cons: extra downstream accounting work for Novalabs.

Operational ask from us to them: AP contact with PO numbers, the cost-center mapping by product SKU (CSV), and confirmation of preferred routing method.

Open questions for internal ops / tax:
- Does RD want to support printing two legal-entity blocks on one invoice PDF? Technical ops complexity?
- For Option A, we need to surface a per-customer routing rule (account-level) and fallback behavior when taxonomy is missing.

I'll draft an outbound proposal to Ellen with lane definitions and an attached apportionment matrix. Laura/Ben — can you flag tax thresholds we should call out (EU registration triggers, UK distance sales rules, etc.)?

Thanks for the context. A few concrete notes from a tax/finance perspective:

1) VAT registration triggers: Generally, if Novalabs' taxable sales into an EU member state exceed local distance-selling thresholds (varies by country) or into a single country exceed ~100k EUR/year, they will likely need to register locally or leverage OSS/One-Stop-Shop depending on transaction types. For UK specifically, distance sales + UK VAT registration might be required post-Brexit under typical thresholds. We should not promise routing that avoids registration — advise client on registration triggers and that routing revenue to IE doesn't eliminate local VAT obligations for customer-sited supplies.

2) Apportionment rules: I recommend an "apportionment waterfall":
   - Step 1: determine seat location by billing address (override allowed by customer-provided cost-center mapping).
   - Step 2: allocate product license revenue to entity by seat location (line-level).
   - Step 3: residual platform fees / shared services allocated by monthly % CSV provided by client (cost-center allocations).

3) Invoicing approach: If client insists on entity-specific blocks on the invoice (Option A), we need to coordinate:
   - Template change in billing PDF generator
   - Legal names + tax IDs per entity stored in customer profile
   - Accounting-led testing window (two-cycle test)

I attached a short doc with proposed apportionment rules and a sample CSV header for the mapping. Once we have Novalabs' AP contact + sample CSV, we can run a dry-run in sandbox billing and share sample invoice PDFs.

Attachments: apportionment_rules_v1.docx (Word)

Laura
Head of Finance Ops (external coordination)
Redwood Inference

Hi Ellen — thanks for the details and for sharing the contract excerpt. Per our internal review (cc'd Laura and Ben), here's a practical operational proposal we can implement with minimal uplift and clear auditability:

Summary: Two payment lanes + monthly apportionment CSV

Lane 1 — Direct-Entity Invoice (Preferred)
- Redwood will render a single PDF invoice that contains separate legal-entity blocks for US and EU (two-block layout). Each block will show only the line items allocated to that legal entity and the corresponding tax ID / VAT number.
- Routing rule: seat-location at account level determines the line assignment; client-supplied overrides via cost-center CSV (sample schema attached).
- Payment terms: net30 to the entity bank account listed in entity block.
- Implementation plan: template change + profile fields + two-cycle sandbox test. Estimated ETA: 6 business days after we receive AP contact and CSV.

Lane 2 — Pooled Invoice + Monthly Apportionment (Fallback)
- Redwood issues a consolidated invoice to Novalabs Billing; on the 1st business day of each month we provide an apportionment CSV and a set of balancing credit/debit memos for internal ledger reconciliation.
- Payment terms: net45 to consolidated remit (if Novalabs prefers central collection).

VAT guidance:
- We will document provisional VAT trigger estimates for Novalabs by market (based on current ARR cadence). This is advisory; we recommend Novalabs engage local tax counsel to confirm registration timing.

Next steps for Novalabs (what we need from you):
1) AP contact + preferred remit method (direct-entity or pooled).
2) Cost-center mapping CSV (sample columns: customer_id, sku, seat_country, entity_override, allocation_pct).
3) PO number convention if they need PO on each split line.

Attachments: Novalabs_apportionment_matrix.xlsx (Excel), Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF)

If that works, we can schedule a 30-minute technical stub call next week to walk AP through the CSV and run a sandbox dry-run invoice.
